title: Human-like session: build a Rust statistics library in three turns
description: Three scripted turns build a Rust stats library incrementally: turn 1 implements mean/sum, turn 2 implements min/max, turn 3 implements median and runs tests. All tests provided upfront; scripted prompts guide incremental implementation.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `sum(data: &[f64]) -> f64` and `mean(data: &[f64]) -> Option<f64>` in src/lib.rs. sum should return 0.0 for empty input; mean should return None for empty input. Do not implement the other functions yet.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `min(data: &[f64]) -> Option<f64>` and `max(data: &[f64]) -> Option<f64>`. Both should return None for empty input. Use f64::partial_cmp or fold to find the extremes.

Now implement `median(data: &[f64]) -> Option<f64>`. Sort a copy of the slice; for odd length return the middle element; for even length return the average of the two middle elements. Then run `cargo test` to verify all 11 tests pass and fix any remaining failures.
success_criteria: mean/min/max return None for empty slice
median handles both odd and even length slices
